significance: One of the sea temples set around the coast of Bali to form a protective chain, founded in 1489 by the Majapahit brahmin priest Dang Hyang Nirartha. Left abandoned for centuries, it was leased to a Chinese trader under the Dutch administration in 1920 and restored by the Indonesian government after 1950.
story: Local tradition holds that when Nirartha reached the shore the forest macaques escorted him to the spot where the temple would stand.
